newsitem.title: USA: Jenny Craig settles deceptive ad charges.
newsitem.headline: Jenny Craig settles deceptive ad charges.

text.p: Jenny Craig Inc. has settled government charges of deceptive advertising for its claims of weight loss, the Federal Trade Commission said Thursday.

"Jenny Craig has agreed not to misrepresent the performance, safety or customer endorsement of any wieght loss programme and to have scientific data to back up future claims," the FTC said in a statement.
The FTC focused on testimonials it said were unrepresentative of the typical experience of Jenny Craig clients.

From now on, claims in most ads will have to include the statement: "For many dieters, weight loss is temporary." It will also have to disclose the average weight loss maintenance for consumers, the commission said.
Testimonials about highly successful maintenance of weight loss would have to be accompanied by the phrase: "This result is not typical. You may be less successful."
The company will also have to more inclusive in its explanation of costs.
In the past, some ads suggested dieters could lose all the weight they wanted for $49, although the actual costs could run into hundreds of dollars.
Jenny Craig, Inc., based in Del Mar, Calif., had no immediate comment.

The FTC vote was 4-0. There will now be 60 days for the public to comment to the FTC, Office of the Secretary, 6th and Pennsylvania Ave. NW, Washington DC 20580. The public can also reach the FTC through the World Wide Web, at http://www.ftc.gov.
